profile.reading:
DartPoints operates a data center at 2425 Technology Boulevard in Columbus, Indiana, a smaller city roughly 40 miles south of Indianapolis, under the company code CLU01 referencing the Columbus, Indiana airport designation, distinct from the more commonly known Columbus, Ohio. This facility traces its origin to Immedion, a Greenville, South Carolina-headquartered colocation provider founded in 2007 that operated eight data centers across seven markets, before DartPoints announced its acquisition of the company on March 16, 2021. The facility spans 86,400 total square feet of slab floor space with an 8,500-square-foot data hall, drawing 2.5 megawatts of utility power against a 735-kilowatt critical IT load, cooled by 300 tons of N+1 redundant capacity, and connecting through 6 on-site network providers. DartPoints markets the building as engineered to withstand EF-5 tornadoes, the most severe rating on the Enhanced Fujita scale, a notable resilience feature given Indiana's exposure to severe Midwest storm systems. No independent local news coverage of this specific facility could be located this session, as an attempt to reach The Republic, the local Columbus, Indiana newspaper, returned an access error, and WebSearch quota was exhausted for the remainder of the session. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed, and no opening year or Uptime Institute Tier certification level is stated on DartPoints' own page for this building.

DartPoints markets itself company-wide as serving more than 900 enterprise customers, including universities, hospital systems, and Fortune 500 companies, and has been recognized on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private US companies in multiple recent years. Across its roughly 11 data centers spanning 5 states, DartPoints reports more than 325,000 total square feet of facility space and more than 20 megawatts of combined power capacity.

reading.body:
DartPoints Columbus publishes 2.5 MW of IT capacity, representing the only megawatt figure disclosed by any data center operator in Indiana, though this reflects a data gap rather than market dominance.

The facility sits in Columbus, Indiana at a regional operator focused on Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets outside major metros. DartPoints operates 11 facilities across 10 states following its April 2025 acquisition by NOVA Infrastructure, which committed more than 250 million dollars in combined growth capital alongside real estate acquisition in three states. The operator emphasizes AI-ready, high-density infrastructure, though the Columbus location's specifications beyond IT capacity remain unpublished.

2.5 MW translates to roughly 63 racks at 40 kW per rack, a density appropriate for AI training workloads, or roughly 250 racks at 10 kW per rack, typical for colocation. Without facility-level electrical specifications or cooling capacity data, the effective density and workload suitability cannot be assessed from published sources. No security certifications are listed, limiting inference about regulated or sensitive workload hosting.

The absence of published capacity figures from five other Indiana data centers means this site cannot rank regional infrastructure by actual supply. The data shows only that DartPoints Columbus chose to disclose, not what the state's total computing footprint comprises.
